newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Turkish, Kurdish youths fight at Rotterdam concert.
newsitem.headline: Turkish, Kurdish youths fight at Rotterdam concert.

text.p: Police fired two warning shots above the heads of hundreds of Turkish and Kurdish youths fighting at a Turkish concert in a Rotterdam suburb on Friday night, the Dutch news agency ANP said.
It said a mass brawl broke out when up to 70 Kurdish youths entered the concert hall in Schiedam, shouting anti-Turkish slogans.
A token police presence was overwhelmed by the ferocity of the fighting and reinforcements had to be called in to separate the two sides and empty the hall.
When the Kurds again tried to storm the hall, one policeman fired two warning shots.
The crowds then dispersed although police said there was further sporadic fighting in the area and witnesses told ANP that up to six shots may have been fired during the night.
Police said they arrested three men in connection with the clashes, in which another five people were slightly hurt.
Deputy Prime Minister Hans Dijkstal said on Thursday that he was concerned at the increasing politicisation of some sectors of the Turkish community in the Netherlands.

Turks and Kurds also clashed briefly in The Hague and in the central Dutch city of Arnhem last Wednesday after the Turkish national soccer team beat the Netherlands 1-0 in a World Cup qualifier in Turkey. Police then made 14 arrests.

Thousands have died in a 12-year conflict between the Turkish military and Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who are fighting for autonomy or independence in the predominantly Kurdish southeast of Turkey.

In a separate development the mayor of The Hague, fearing trouble, called off a peace march planned for Sunday to protest the deaths of a Turkish immigrant mother and five of her children in a suspected arson attack on their Hague home last month.
Ankara has sharply criticised the Dutch and German authorities for failing to punish western perpetrators of suspected anti-Moslem attacks.
